answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, withdrawable stake before it may submit bids, with a portion slashed when a randomly audited claim proves fraudulent. Splitting one attacker’s budget across many identities does not create more total influence: every fake agent must fund its own stake, and detectable fraud burns capital. The inlet can accept claims, while a jade ledger records deposits and slashing; an honest agent may wander between tasks without losing its stake. The cost is tied to the attacker’s attempt to gain influence, not merely to creating names.
